<summary>Combien produit 1 kWc de pannea: <summary>How much does 1 kWp of solar panels produce in Luxembourg?</summary>
Environ 1 070 kWh par an pour un toit pl: About 1,070 kWh a year for a due-south roof pitched at 35° in Luxembourg City (PVGIS, 2005-2023 average, 14% system losses), 1,010 kWh for a south-east or south-west roof, 860 kWh for an east or west roof. The north of the country (Clervaux, Wiltz) produces 3% less, the south (Esch, Capellen) 2% more. A 6 kWp system therefore produces 5,500 to 6,400 kWh a year, 1.4 to 1.6 times the consumption of an average household (3,900 kWh).
<summary>Quel est le montant du Klimabon: <summary>How much is the Klimabonus for solar PV in 2026?</summary>
Pour une installation en autoconsommatio: For a self-consumption system of power P (in kWp, at least 2), mounted on the roof or façade or integrated into the building envelope, the subsidy is P × (1,155 − 33 × P) euros below 15 kWp and 10,000 euros from 15 kWp: €__KB3__ for 3 kWp, €__KB6__ for 6 kWp, €__KB10__ for 10 kWp. A battery of capacity Q (kWh) adds Q × (500 − 500/18 × Q) euros, €2,250 from 9 kWh. The subsidy can be deducted from the invoice by an installer listed in the register of intermediary applicants (pre-financing, optional) or claimed afterwards through the standard procedure. Eligible invoices: 4 January 2026 to 31 December 2029, or up to 31 December 2031 if the system was ordered by 31 December 2029 at the latest. Condition: waive any guaranteed remuneration for the electricity fed in. Since 1 October 2026 (invoice date), an energy management system (HEMS) that controls at least two devices (panels, battery, heat pump, charging station, controllable immersion heater) also receives €500.
<summary>Klimabonus ou tarif d'injection: <summary>Klimabonus or guaranteed feed-in tariff: which to choose?</summary>
Les deux ne se cumulent pas. Le Klimabon: The two cannot be combined. The Klimabonus cuts the upfront investment and suits small or medium systems that self-consume a good share of their output. The guaranteed tariff (__TAR26__ c€/kWh for a first feed-in in 2026, __TAR27__ c€ in 2027, for 15 years, up to 10 kW) pays better for the surplus and becomes competitive when the system is large relative to consumption. Tool 2 computes both for your case; as a rule, the more you feed in, the closer option B gets to option A. For an offer signed between 1 October 2024 and 4 March 2026, a transitional scheme lets you combine the guaranteed tariff with a 20% subsidy capped at €500/kWp, provided the final invoice is dated 31 December 2026 at the latest (Klima-Agence, 17 December 2025); this scheme is not simulated here.
<summary>Combien coûte une installation: <summary>How much does a solar PV system cost in Luxembourg?</summary>
Les devis 2026 relevés chez les installa: 2026 quotes seen from installers range from €1,600 to €2,200 per kWp installed for 6 to 15 kWp, i.e. €__C6LO__ to €__C6HI__ for 6 kWp, VAT included. Supply and installation on a dwelling qualifies for the super-reduced VAT rate of 3%. After the Klimabonus, a 6 kWp system costs about €__NET6LO__ to €__NET6HI__.
Seules les composantes variables de la f: Only the variable components of the bill are avoided: energy (about 13 c€/kWh in 2026), the grid's volumetric charge (5.10 c€), the compensation mechanism (−3.71 c€ from August to December 2026 thanks to temporary State aid, −0.10 c€ from January to July), the electricity tax (0.10 c€), all subject to 8% VAT: about 16 c€/kWh from August to December 2026, and close to 20 c€ at the January to July 2026 tariff, which still includes a State contribution; the 2027 tariff is not published as of 2 November 2026. Fixed charges (metering, reference power) remain due. Counting 25 c€ because "my bill divided by my kWh gives 25 cents" overstates the gain.
Une batterie fait passer la part autocon: A battery lifts the self-consumed share from about 30% to 50-60% for a typical house, but costs €700 to €1,100 per kWh installed (an indicative range assumed by the tool, with no published source; €900 by default), part of which the Klimabonus refunds (up to €2,250). With a surplus sold at 5 c€ and an avoided kWh worth 20 c€, each stored kWh earns 15 c€: a 7 kWh battery cycled 250 times a year earns about €260 a year for €__BAT7LO__ to €__BAT7HI__ of net investment after the Klimabonus. It therefore usually lengthens the payback time; tool 2 shows it for your case.
<summary>Les revenus d'une installation: <summary>Is the income from a solar PV system taxable?</summary>
Pour une personne physique exploitant un: For a private individual operating a system of 1 to 30 kWp, the direct tax administration accepts, as a matter of tolerance, that it is a hobby activity not counted in taxable income (circular L.I.R. no. 14/2 of 5 June 2023, summarised by Klima-Agence). With pure self-consumption there is no commercial activity at all.

<strong>Calcul.</strong> Production = pu: Calculation. Production = power × PVGIS yield (orientation, pitch) × canton factor, spread by month along the PVGIS profile for Luxembourg City. Self-consumed share without battery = 30% × (production ÷ consumption)−0.6, bounded between 10 and 90%; a battery of Q kWh adds 35% × (1 − e−Q ÷ (0.5 × daily consumption)). Annual gain = self-consumed kWh × value of the avoided kWh (indexed by the chosen rise) + kWh fed in × surplus price (option A) or guaranteed tariff for 15 years then surplus price (option B). Production declines at the chosen ageing rate; the inverter is replaced in year 13. Payback time = first year in which the cumulative cash flow turns positive (interpolated); net gain = cumulative cash flow at 25 years in nominal euros, undiscounted by default (with a discount rate: sum of the discounted flows; payback time and figure 2 remain undiscounted); IRR = rate that sets the present value of the flows to zero. No maintenance or insurance cost is counted. The self-consumption formula is a heuristic specific to this calculator, set to the order of magnitude of 30% without a battery, with no published reference. The battery is neither replaced nor degraded over 25 years: with a battery, the result is optimistic. The optional HEMS is counted as a cost and, in option A only, with its subsidy; its effect on the self-consumed share is not modelled.

Hourly heat pump COP = __COP_F__ × (__COP_A__ − __COP_B__ ΔT + __COP_C__ ΔT²), at least 1, where ΔT is the gap between the flow temperature and the outdoor temperature T, taken as at least __COP_DTMIN__ °C (formula of Ruhnau et al., 2019, correction factor included); flow at 40 − T °C (radiators) or 30 − 0.5 × T °C (underfloor heating), hot water at 50 °C; a direct electric back-up covers whatever the available output does not. The buffer tank is heated 15 °C above the flow temperature with the solar surplus (1.163 Wh per litre per °C, losses of 1% per hour) and releases its heat when the panels no longer suffice. Battery: 90% round-trip efficiency, 0.5 kW per kWh, 5 kW at most. Bill = fuel + electricity bought − surplus sold + maintenance (boiler €200/year, heat pump €150/year); fuel rises at the chosen rate, electricity as in tool 2; with panels, the inverter is replaced in year 13. Payback and net gain = spending difference with the current heating over __HORIZON_H__ years. Limits: a single weather year, no panel ageing or battery replacement in this tool, single-family houses only, cancelled gas standing charge not counted, municipal grants not counted.
